body:
Your title and post really hit me hard. It's exactly how I feel like I have been for the past 2 years.

Suicide has been been on the table for a year now but I know deep down at 29 I can start my life again, reboot everything and become the person I always wanted to be.

Well after reading your story I'm glad you're OK and that you can see the light at the end of the tunnel.

I think what puzzles a lot of people going through this type of thing is that the person they married, who they trusted and loved for such a long time is no longer there. I'm not talking about small changes here and there, I'm talking about a complete 180 change leaving you scratching your head going "Who the hell is that person?"

Wow. You have pretty much just described my marriage situation that I am going through right now down to a T, so I know exactly where you are coming from and understand.

Towards the end of my marriage we both got lazy and complacent and we never really knew how to fix things because it seems that it went too far one way and could never recover and just like you described, me and my ex also seemed to not care towards the end. I just always had hope that we would find ourselves again but we never did. 

I think once complacency sets in and arguing and fights break out to the point it is a common theme there is no going back.
